solutionSource.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

entries.clue: It’s a festival — knock back one tot and lots of weed (5,4)

indicatorNotes.knock back: to knock back a drink is to down it, and read as 'send back' it turns the phrase round
indicatorNotes.lots of: lots of the weed but not all of it, so the final letter is left off

blocks.note: one = I and a dram is a tot of whisky; I DRAM is turned round
grass is slang for cannabis; drop its last letter

annotation.surface: Someone at a party downs a drink and has a smoke.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Knock back' sounds like drinking, which suits the tot, but here it turns I DRAM round.
annotation.definitionFit: The French name, 'fat Tuesday', is the carnival held before Lent, most famously in New Orleans.

entries.clue: Old barrel organ, microphone covering unserviceable on crate (5,3)

indicatorNotes.covering: to cover something is to wrap round it, so MIC wraps round US
indicatorNotes.on: in a down clue, one part sitting on another is written above it

annotation.surface: A junk dealer describes a clapped-out organ sitting on a crate with a microphone.
annotation.walkthrough: US for unserviceable is a crossword abbreviation worth learning.
annotation.definitionFit: Both are mechanical players that pick out a tune from a pinned revolving cylinder; a barrel organ is the older, larger kind.

entries.clue: Discharge ambassador into the booze (5)

indicatorNotes.into: putting one thing into another places it inside, so the ambassador goes inside the booze

blocks.note: rum as a general word for drink
HE = His Excellency, an ambassador's title

annotation.surface: An ambassador is thrown out for being drunk.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Discharge' reads as dismissal from a post, which fits the drunken ambassador, but it is the noun: a watery flow.
annotation.definitionFit: The word names the watery mucus that runs from the eyes or nose, a bodily discharge.

entries.clue: Do I pair individual parts? (11)

indicatorNotes.parts: to part something is to split it, and MATE is split to let PERSON in

blocks.note: to pair animals is to mate them

annotation.surface: Someone wonders whether to split up a pair.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Parts' looks like a noun in a question about pairs, but it is the verb that splits MATE open.
annotation.definitionFit: Do in the sense of mimicking someone: 'he does a great Elvis'.

entries.clue: Maybe Reading team screening YouTube finally live (6)

indicatorNotes.Maybe: maybe marks reading as one example of a set, here the three Rs
indicatorNotes.screening: a screen stands in front and hides, so R SIDE hides the E inside it
indicatorNotes.finally: finally points to the end of the word, its last letter

blocks.note: reading is one of the three Rs

annotation.surface: Reading's football club won't show its match live on YouTube.
annotation.walkthrough: Reading is an English town with a football club, which is the picture; here it is one of the three Rs (reading, writing, arithmetic).
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: where you live is where you have your home.

entries.clue: Dark force that might run an undercover Sting? (6,6)

annotation.definition: Dark force that might run an undercover Sting?

blocks.note: a sinister, hidden force of the state

blocks.clueFragment: that might run an undercover Sting?
blocks.note: a sting is a police trap; with its capital, Sting is also the singer of the band The Police

annotation.surface: A shadowy force sets up an undercover trap.
annotation.walkthrough: An undercover Sting would be a hidden member of the Police, so the band pun and the trap both point at SECRET POLICE.
annotation.definitionFit: A state's covert force that spies on its own people is sinister enough to be called dark.

entries.clue: Aphorism from private detective probing Mrs Simpson after retirement (7)

indicatorNotes.probing: a probe pokes into something, so the detective goes inside the name
indicatorNotes.after retirement: to retire is to withdraw backwards, so the name is turned round

blocks.note: Marge Simpson of The Simpsons, turned round

annotation.surface: A private eye digs into Wallis Simpson's life once she has retired.
annotation.walkthrough: Mrs Simpson suggests Wallis Simpson, for whom Edward VIII gave up the throne; the cartoon mother Marge is the one wanted.
annotation.definitionFit: A near-synonym: both name a short, pithy saying, the epigram usually a witty one.

entries.clue: Land reportedly more rocky beneath earth’s surface (7)

indicatorNotes.reportedly: what is reported is heard, so we want a sound rather than a spelling
indicatorNotes.beneath: in a down clue, one part beneath another is written below it
indicatorNotes.surface: a surface is the outermost layer, so earth's surface is its first letter

blocks.note: the comparative of stony; spoken without a final R, as in most British accents

annotation.surface: A report says the ground gets rockier under the topsoil.
annotation.walkthrough: The sound match works in British speech, where the final R of STONIER is not pronounced, so it rhymes with the end of ESTONIA.
annotation.definitionFit: Land in the sense of a country: this one is a Baltic state.

entries.clue: Blissfully happy Viennese haven’t worked — stifling hot (2,7,6)

indicatorNotes.worked: something worked has been kneaded or reshaped, so the letters are rearranged
indicatorNotes.stifling: to stifle is to smother, so the rearranged letters close round H

blocks.note: H = hot, as on a tap

annotation.surface: Cheerful people in Vienna skip work in the heat.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Worked' reads as having a job, and 'stifling hot' as the weather; both are instructions.
annotation.definitionFit: An idiom: the seventh heaven was the highest in old cosmology, so being there means utter bliss.

entries.clue: I boo sorry, awful northern singer (3,7)

indicatorNotes.awful: an awful state is a mess, and messed-up letters are rearranged

annotation.surface: A concertgoer apologises for booing a dreadful singer from the north.
annotation.walkthrough: The heckler's apology reads naturally, so 'awful' passes as a comment on the singing.
annotation.definitionFit: Definition by example: the American who sang 'Oh, Pretty Woman' and 'Crying'.

entries.clue: Fortified island, fortified wine (7)

blocks.note: a Portuguese Atlantic island, ringed with old forts
a wine strengthened with brandy, named after where it is made

annotation.surface: A list of two things that have been fortified.
annotation.walkthrough: The repeated 'fortified' is the trick: once it means defended with forts, once it means strengthened with brandy.
annotation.definitionFit: The Portuguese island gives its name to the brandy-strengthened wine made there, so one word covers both.

entries.clue: Leaders in Middle East celebrate centenary at holy city (5)

indicatorNotes.Leaders in: the leader of a word is the letter at its front, so take the first letter of each word that follows

blocks.note: first letters of Middle, East, celebrate, centenary, at

annotation.surface: Leaders from the region mark a hundred years at a sacred site.
annotation.walkthrough: The surface is fully sensible news copy, and the answer really is in the Middle East.
annotation.definitionFit: The birthplace of Muhammad in Saudi Arabia is the holiest site in Islam.

entries.clue: WWII general sat on snake, which made us laugh (5,6)

indicatorNotes.sat on: in a down clue, whatever sits on something is written above it

annotation.surface: A wartime general sits on a snake, and everyone laughs.
annotation.walkthrough: The absurd scene is itself the kind of sketch the answer would write. Monty Python was the British comedy team behind Flying Circus.
annotation.definitionFit: Definition by description: the comedy troupe's whole job was to make audiences laugh.

entries.clue: Links hosting one European newspaper head (9)

indicatorNotes.hosting: a host has guests inside the house, so CHAIN holds the other pieces

blocks.note: a chain is made of links

annotation.surface: A golf course hosts the editor of a European newspaper.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Links' suggests a golf course, the picture the surface paints; here it is a chain.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym in the tribal sense: the leader of a clan.

entries.clue: Goddess beginning to get seen in A&E (7)

indicatorNotes.seen in: to be seen in a place is to be inside it, as a patient is seen in a hospital department

blocks.note: the two letters that hold the rest

annotation.surface: A goddess waits to be seen in a hospital emergency department.
annotation.walkthrough: A&E is Accident and Emergency, the British hospital casualty department; only its two letters are used.
annotation.definitionFit: Definition by example: the Phoenician deity of fertility and love.

entries.clue: Guides that woman’s dad through southern Sierra (7)

indicatorNotes.through: something passing through runs inside, so HER PA sits between the two S's

blocks.note: Sierra is S in the NATO alphabet

annotation.surface: Guides take a woman's father across a mountain range in the south.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Sierra' paints a mountain range to fit the guides; it is just S from the radio alphabet.
annotation.definitionFit: The Himalayan people are so associated with mountain guiding that their name is used for any guide.

entries.clue: Traitor caught next to case of explosives — Times (7)

indicatorNotes.case of: a case is the outside that holds the contents, so take the outer letters

blocks.note: at = next to, as in 'at the door'
first and last letters of explosives
times = by, as in three by four

annotation.surface: A newspaper headline about a traitor caught beside a box of explosives.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Times' looks like the newspaper; it is the multiplication sign. The explosives fit the answer's story.
annotation.definitionFit: Definition by example: Robert Catesby led the 1605 Gunpowder Plot to blow up Parliament.

entries.clue: Depression is beginning to torment one filling in at work (7)

indicatorNotes.beginning to: the beginning of a word is its first letter

annotation.surface: Someone's low mood torments a temp covering at the office.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Filling in at work' reads as covering for a colleague; the fillings are in teeth.
annotation.definitionFit: A cryptic description: this professional's daily work is putting fillings in.

entries.clue: Harvard, say, where the students like to take a punt? (9,10)

annotation.definition2: where the students like to take a punt

blocks.note: Harvard is a university in a Massachusetts town named after an English one

blocks.clueFragment: where the students like to take a punt
blocks.note: punting, pushing a flat boat with a pole, is a famous student pastime on the river Cam

annotation.surface: A question about whether Harvard students are gamblers.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Take a punt' is British slang for having a go or a bet, but a punt is also a flat boat.
annotation.definitionFit: Harvard sits in Cambridge, Massachusetts, while the English university town is famous for punting on the Cam.

entries.clue: Father packs uniform coat (3)

indicatorNotes.packs: to pack something is to put it inside, so FR holds U

blocks.note: Uniform is U in the NATO alphabet

annotation.surface: A priest packs his uniform and coat.
annotation.walkthrough: The surface is a priest packing clothes, so uniform and coat both look like garments; uniform is just the letter U.
annotation.definitionFit: An animal's coat is its hair, and a coat made from that hair is also called by the answer.

entries.clue: Best remote US broadcaster (6)

blocks.note: remote = out of the way, as in outlying

annotation.surface: A verdict on which American TV channel is the top remote pick.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Best' looks like an adjective praising a broadcaster, but it is the verb: to beat.
annotation.definitionFit: Best as a verb means to get the better of someone, which is to outwit them.

entries.clue: Florentines succeeded under trade union scrutiny (7)

indicatorNotes.under: in a down clue, whatever is under something is written below it

annotation.surface: Workers from Florence came through a union investigation.
annotation.walkthrough: S for succeeded comes from family trees, where it marks who followed whom.
annotation.definitionFit: Florence is the capital of Tuscany, so its citizens are people of that region.

entries.clue: Country run stops painful injury (6)

indicatorNotes.stops: a stopper plugs a hole, so R plugs the inside of the country

annotation.surface: A country's winning run is halted by an injury.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Stops' reads as the injury ending a run; it is a container.
annotation.definitionFit: A wrenched ankle or wrist is the classic example, and it hurts.

entries.clue: Carried by some piece of luggage whatever happens? (2,3,4)

blocks.note: what is carried by something is in it
any = some, as in 'have you any bread?'

annotation.surface: Something travels in a bag, come what may.
annotation.walkthrough: The wordplay reads almost literally as the answer, which is why the question mark is there.
annotation.definitionFit: An idiom meaning regardless or come what may.

entries.clue: City poet, following change of heart, cross (8)

indicatorNotes.change of heart: the heart is the middle of a word, and changing it rearranges those letters

blocks.note: a poet is a bard; its heart, AR, is changed round
to ford a river is to cross it

annotation.surface: A poet, having changed his mind, is angry with a city.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Cross' reads as angry, but it is the verb meaning to wade across.
annotation.definitionFit: Definition by example: a large wool-trade city in West Yorkshire, England.

entries.clue: Soft Shoe Shuffle April, Leeds (10)

indicatorNotes.Shuffle: to shuffle cards is to mix them, so the letters are mixed

annotation.surface: An advert for a soft-shoe dance show in Leeds in April.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Soft Shoe Shuffle' is a dance, so the eye reads it as one phrase; split it into the definition and the anagram signal.
annotation.definitionFit: A light canvas shoe with a rope sole is about as soft as footwear gets.

entries.clue: Actor trained to breathe lazily (9,6)

indicatorNotes.trained: something trained is shaped into a new form, as a plant is trained along a wall

annotation.surface: An actor has been taught to breathe in a relaxed way.
annotation.walkthrough: Drama students do learn breathing, so 'trained' sits naturally in the surface.
annotation.definitionFit: Definition by example: the Hollywood star of Cleopatra and Cat on a Hot Tin Roof.

entries.clue: Cheer hospital nurse Rosemary after clearing out braying toff (6,5)

indicatorNotes.after clearing out: clearing out a room empties its middle, so Rosemary keeps only its outside letters

blocks.note: H = hospital, as on road signs

annotation.surface: A hospital nurse called Rosemary is cheered after throwing out a loud, posh visitor.
annotation.walkthrough: The answer is British slang for a loud, upper-class young man. EN is the crossword's enrolled nurse.
annotation.definitionFit: British slang for a loud upper-class young man; toff is slang for a posh person, and braying mocks the voice.

entries.clue: Ninja, modish, led by a pair of donkeys? (8)

indicatorNotes.led by: whatever leads goes in front, so the donkeys come before IN

annotation.surface: A fashionable ninja rides behind a pair of donkeys.
annotation.walkthrough: The image of a ninja led by donkeys is deliberately silly, and the question mark admits it.
annotation.definitionFit: Definition by example: ninjas were Japanese covert agents hired to spy and to kill.

entries.clue: National bet (6)

blocks.note: a noun here: a citizen of a country, in this case the USA
a British bookmaker's multiple bet on four selections in eleven combinations

annotation.walkthrough: 'National' also suggests the Grand National horse race, which sits nicely beside 'bet'.
annotation.definitionFit: The word is slang for an American citizen and also the name of a four-horse accumulator bet.

entries.clue: No time for quarrel with male journalist outside, somewhat offended (6)

indicatorNotes.No time for: no time means the T is taken away
indicatorNotes.outside: M and ED stand on the outside, round the rest

blocks.note: a tiff is a quarrel; remove T

annotation.surface: A busy journalist has no time to argue with a man and is a bit put out.
annotation.walkthrough: 'No time for' reads as being too busy; it deletes T.
annotation.definitionFit: The word describes mild annoyance, a step short of real offence.

entries.clue: Picture that is used as cover for magazine (5)

indicatorNotes.used as cover for: a cover goes round what it protects, so IE wraps round MAG

annotation.surface: A picture is chosen for a magazine's cover.
annotation.walkthrough: The surface nearly describes the answer, which sits on a magazine cover.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: a visual representation of something.

entries.clue: Hide ecstasy inside gadget from the east after daughter did (8)

indicatorNotes.Hide: to hide something is to tuck it away inside something else
indicatorNotes.inside: confirms where the ecstasy is hidden: within the gadget
indicatorNotes.from the east: east is on the right of a map, so read from the right, backwards
indicatorNotes.after: in an across clue, whatever comes after something is written to its right, so the turned gadget follows D

annotation.surface: Someone hides drugs in a gadget, just as his daughter did.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Did' is the definition, in the slang sense of cheated: 'he did me out of fifty quid'. It sits last and looks like padding.
annotation.definitionFit: Slang: to do someone is to swindle them, so did is the past tense of cheating.

entries.clue: Timeless lawsuit involving tabloid paper in the capital (8)

indicatorNotes.Timeless: without time, so the T is removed
indicatorNotes.involving: to involve is to take in, so ACION takes SUN inside

blocks.note: a lawsuit is an action; remove T
The Sun, a British tabloid newspaper

annotation.surface: An endless court case in the capital involves a tabloid newspaper.
annotation.walkthrough: 'The capital' reads as London, home of the tabloids, but here it means any capital, in this case in South America.
annotation.definitionFit: Definition by example: it is the capital city of Paraguay.

entries.clue: Matching dishes perhaps left here, we’re told (2,5)

indicatorNotes.we’re told: what we are told is spoken, so we want a sound rather than a spelling

blocks.note: where dirty dishes are left in the kitchen

annotation.surface: A remark about where unwashed dishes get left.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Matching' could describe a set of dishes, which is the misleading picture; the definition means moving together in time.
annotation.definitionFit: Short for synchronised: two things keeping time with each other match.

entries.clue: Pliable state of Pat & Lydia, a bit tipsy (12)

indicatorNotes.tipsy: a tipsy person reels about, so the letters reel into a new order

blocks.note: anagram fodder, 12 letters; the ampersand only joins the names

annotation.surface: Pat and Lydia are a bit drunk and going along with anything.
annotation.walkthrough: The tipsy pair are agreeable, which gives the surface a hint of the answer.
annotation.definitionFit: Being pliable means bending to fit circumstances, the quality the noun names.

entries.clue: Paradoxical burger? (4,4)

blocks.note: a paradox seems to contradict itself; think of another sense of going without meals
the question mark flags that a burger is one example

annotation.walkthrough: To fast is to go without eating, so fast food sounds like a contradiction, yet a burger is exactly that.
annotation.definitionFit: A burger is the classic quick-service meal, and the name contradicts itself if fast means abstaining.

entries.clue: Express no longer on this quick route (5,6)

blocks.note: fleet = fast, as in fleet of foot

annotation.surface: An express train no longer runs on a fast line.
annotation.walkthrough: Express is the Daily Express newspaper, not a train. The answer is the London street that housed the national press until the 1980s.
annotation.definitionFit: The Daily Express once had its offices on this London street, as the national newspapers did, and moved away.

entries.clue: Mr Klein dropping in, rejected soda for something stronger (8)

indicatorNotes.dropping: to drop something is to let it go, so IN is let go from his first name
indicatorNotes.rejected: something rejected is sent back, so SODA is written backwards

blocks.note: Calvin Klein, the fashion designer, without IN

annotation.surface: Calvin Klein drops by, turns down a soft drink and asks for a real one.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Dropping in' reads as visiting; it tells you to drop the letters IN.
annotation.definitionFit: An apple brandy from Normandy is much stronger than soda, the drink the clue rejects.

entries.clue: Way into pastry dish that’s frozen (5)

annotation.definitionNote: the definition leans on 'Way' too: a way that is frozen

indicatorNotes.into: putting one thing into another places it inside, so ST goes inside PIE

annotation.surface: A path leads into a frozen pie.
annotation.walkthrough: 'That's frozen' seems to describe the pie, but it describes the answer: a snowy ski run.
annotation.definitionFit: A ski run is a way over packed snow and ice, frozen by definition.

entries.clue: Room willing for charades? (7,4)

annotation.surface: Someone asks whether there's a room and the will for a game of charades.
annotation.walkthrough: The question mark marks charades as one example of the answer.
annotation.definitionFit: Definition by example: charades is a traditional indoor group game played in a sitting room.

entries.clue: Pleasant housing over road that’s within budget (10)

indicatorNotes.housing: a house holds its occupants, so AFFABLE holds O and RD

annotation.surface: An estate agent praises pleasant, cheap homes by a road.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Housing' and 'within budget' together suggest cheap homes; housing is the container signal.
annotation.definitionFit: Something you can pay for without overspending is cheap enough to buy.

entries.clue: Tight deadline of English writer (6,5)

indicatorNotes.Tight: tight is slang for drunk, and drunk letters reel into a new order

annotation.surface: An English author is working to a strict deadline.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Tight deadline' is a stock phrase, so 'tight' hides as an adjective.
annotation.definitionFit: Definition by example: the English author of Robinson Crusoe.

entries.clue: Knight blocking list I’m on upset political sponsor (9)

indicatorNotes.blocking: a block stands in the way in the middle, so N goes inside
indicatorNotes.upset: in a down clue, upset turns the letters upside down, which reverses them

blocks.note: a rota is a list of duties

annotation.surface: A knight on a list of candidates upsets the party that proposed him.
annotation.walkthrough: N is the chess knight, because K is already taken by the king.
annotation.definitionFit: Someone who puts a candidate forward for office is sponsoring them.

entries.clue: Downy cloth Family Circle tableware item (6,4)

blocks.note: the soft raised surface of a fabric

annotation.surface: A catalogue listing a soft cloth set for the family table.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Downy cloth' suggests the napkin itself; it is only the fluffy surface of a fabric.
annotation.definitionFit: A band that holds a rolled table napkin is set out with the cutlery and plates.

entries.clue: Record second effort platinum-selling album (8)

annotation.surface: A musician makes a second attempt at a hit album.
annotation.walkthrough: The music-business surface hides that 'Record' is the verb.
annotation.definitionFit: Definition by example: Carole King's 1971 album is one of the best-selling records ever.

entries.clue: Phantom at ill-omened gathering a Mexican favourite (9)

indicatorNotes.gathering: to gather is to collect, so the words collect the answer inside them

blocks.note: the letters run from the end of Phantom into ill-omened

annotation.surface: A ghost at a sinister gathering is a Mexican crowd-pleaser.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Gathering' looks like a noun for a meeting, but it is the verb.
annotation.definitionFit: The small green husked fruit is central to Mexican salsa verde.

entries.clue: Rifleman’s told this way to get to Edinburgh? (4,3)

blocks.note: the order a marksman is given before firing
an instruction to drive on the A1(M), with the 1 read as a letter

annotation.surface: A soldier is given directions to Scotland's capital.
annotation.walkthrough: The A1(M) is the motorway stretch of the A1, the main road from London to Edinburgh. Written TAKE A1M, the 1 stands for I.
annotation.definitionFit: A rifleman is told to point his gun at the target, and the same words send a driver up the A1(M).

entries.clue: Youth absent touring India made redundant (4,3)

indicatorNotes.touring: a tour goes all the way round a place, so LAD goes round I

blocks.note: India is I in the NATO alphabet

annotation.surface: A young man misses work to go travelling in India and loses his job.
annotation.walkthrough: The gap-year picture is complete in the surface; India is just the letter I.
annotation.definitionFit: Two ways of saying someone has lost their job because it no longer exists.

entries.clue: Plant-based cure containing skin of rhubarb (6)

indicatorNotes.containing: to contain is to hold inside, so HEAL holds RB
indicatorNotes.skin of: the skin is the outside, so take the outer letters

blocks.note: first and last letters of rhubarb

annotation.surface: A plant remedy made with rhubarb peel.
annotation.walkthrough: The surface is a folk remedy and the answer belongs in it; 'cure' is a verb here.
annotation.definitionFit: Made from herbs, which are plants, as a remedy or tea might be.

entries.clue: Living as a pensioner, given a minor internal adjustment, heard again (7)

indicatorNotes.given a minor internal adjustment: a small change inside the word, here two middle letters swapping places

annotation.surface: A pensioner has a small operation and gets their hearing checked again.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Heard again' is legal: a case is heard in court. Only I and R swap.
annotation.definitionFit: A court case that is tried a second time is heard again.

entries.clue: He’s booked to appear before Judges (6)

annotation.definition: He’s booked to appear before Judges

blocks.note: a man who has a book named after him, in the Old Testament
Judges is a book of the Bible; look at the one before it

annotation.surface: A defendant is due to appear in court.
annotation.walkthrough: The courtroom picture is false: 'booked' means has a Bible book, and Judges is the next book.
annotation.definitionFit: In the Old Testament, the book named for Moses's successor comes immediately before Judges.

entries.clue: Underworld head, very large flag (6)

blocks.note: a flag is a kind of this plant

annotation.surface: A crime boss flies a huge flag.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Flag' is the plant, the yellow flag, not a banner. 'Underworld head' suggests a gangster.
annotation.definitionFit: The Egyptian god who ruled the land of the dead is its head.

entries.clue: Endlessly generous people (3)

indicatorNotes.Endlessly: without an end, so the last letter is cut off

blocks.note: a four-letter word for generous, with its last letter cut

annotation.surface: A tribute to boundlessly generous folk.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Endlessly generous' reads as praise; KIND loses its final D.
annotation.definitionFit: One's people means one's family or relatives.

entries.clue: LibDems cover? (5-5,9)

blocks.note: the Liberal Democrats, long placed behind Labour and the Conservatives in British politics

annotation.walkthrough: The LibDems are traditionally Britain's third party, so their cover would be the minimum kind of motor insurance.
annotation.definitionFit: The minimum UK motor cover pays for damage to others, and the LibDems are the third party of politics.

entries.clue: Nymph — primarily aquatic — featured in North American papers (5)

indicatorNotes.primarily: primarily means first of all, so the first letter
indicatorNotes.featured in: something featured in a paper appears inside it, so A goes inside ID

annotation.surface: A water nymph appears in American newspapers.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Papers' suggests newspapers; here it means identity documents.
annotation.definitionFit: In Greek myth this is a water nymph, so aquatic fits too.

entries.clue: Rough Trade firm backs design movement (3,4)

indicatorNotes.Rough: something roughed up is knocked out of shape, so the letters are rearranged
indicatorNotes.backs: a backer stands behind, so CO comes after

annotation.surface: A record label, Rough Trade, supports a design movement.
annotation.walkthrough: Rough Trade is a real London record label, which is why the two words read as a name.
annotation.definitionFit: Definition by example: the geometric style of the 1920s and 1930s in buildings and objects.

entries.clue: Pancake fed the Spanish painter (7)

indicatorNotes.fed: what is fed goes inside, so the pancake takes in the Spanish word

annotation.surface: A Spanish painter is fed a pancake.
annotation.walkthrough: 'The Spanish' is read as people; it is the Spanish word for the.
annotation.definitionFit: Definition by example: Giovanni Bellini was a Venetian Renaissance master.

entries.clue: Pragmatic person starts to rank every category of celebs (7)

indicatorNotes.starts to: the start of each word is its first letter

blocks.note: first letters of rank and every
the A-list, the top tier of celebrities

annotation.surface: A practical person begins ranking every level of celebrity.
annotation.walkthrough: The A-list is the top category of celebrities, above the B-list.
annotation.definitionFit: Someone who accepts things as they are and acts practically.

entries.clue: Deserve credit (5)

blocks.note: a verb: to be worthy of something
a noun: praise or worth earned

annotation.walkthrough: The two words sit together like a phrase, 'deserve credit', which hides that they are two definitions.
annotation.definitionFit: The word is both a verb for being worthy and a noun for the worth itself.

entries.clue: Chernobyl at last due for new reactor component (4,3)

indicatorNotes.at last: at the last means at the end, so the final letter
indicatorNotes.new: made new means remade, so the letters are rearranged

annotation.surface: Chernobyl is finally due a new part for its reactor.
annotation.walkthrough: The Chernobyl disaster is the picture, and the answer belongs in it.
annotation.definitionFit: A sealed tube of nuclear fuel forms part of a reactor's core.

entries.clue: 27 couple adopting dearest mongrel recently (9)

indicatorNotes.adopting: to adopt is to take in, so the two Ys take the rest inside
indicatorNotes.mongrel: a mongrel is of mixed breed, so the letters are mixed

blocks.note: 27 down is a NATO alphabet word standing for Y; a couple is two

annotation.surface: A couple have lately adopted a beloved mongrel.
annotation.walkthrough: The cross-reference '27' means the answer to 27 down, YANKEE, which is the radio-alphabet word for Y.
annotation.definitionFit: Used loosely, as in 'it seems like only yesterday', it means not long ago.
